app_summary: An online shop selling astronomy products, based on the OpenTelemetry Demo. It is built with polyglot microservices (Go, Java, .NET, Python, Node.js, Rust, ...) communicating via gRPC and HTTP behind an Envoy frontend-proxy, with Kafka for asynchronous order processing and Valkey as cart store. Supported Operations: View product catalog, Receive product recommendations and ads, Add item to cart, Checkout with selected items, Currency conversion, Process payment, Generate shipping quotes, Send order confirmation emails

final_report.root_cause: frontend-proxy (Envoy) attempted connections to a stale ClusterIP (10.96.249.217:8080) that no longer had a listening backend, producing immediate ECONNREFUSED. The proxy was resolving/using an out-of-date address (likely from stale Envoy cluster configuration or cached DNS/ClusterIP) instead of the current frontend Service ClusterIP (10.96.115.5 -> endpoint 10.244.1.16:8080). This caused fast connection failures from frontend-proxy to the frontend backend. The timing indicates the Service IP changed (or service/endpoint was re-created) and the proxy continued to use the old address until its configuration/DNS cache was refreshed or rotated.
affected_resources: old ClusterIP 10.96.249.217:8080 (observed in traces as connection target)
clients: frontend-web (observed in trace spans calling frontend-proxy)
final_report.evidence_summary: 1) Two traces show frontend-proxy failing to fetch backend with error 'connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.249.217:8080' (fast failures). 2) frontend-proxy pod exists and is Running (frontend-proxy-55b6b6c7d9-gbhp8) but its available logs (last 5,000 lines) contain only Envoy startup/initialization entries and no ECONNREFUSED entries or references to 10.96.249.217. 3) frontend-proxy configuration (env) points to 'frontend:8080'. 4) The current frontend Service ClusterIP is 10.96.115.5 with an endpoint at 10.244.1.16:8080 and the frontend pod is healthy and serving (no bind/listen errors). 5) The refused IP (10.96.249.217) does not match the current ClusterIP (10.96.115.5) => indicates some component was using a stale ClusterIP.
final_report.investigation_summary: Priority-1: checked frontend-proxy pods and logs — only one pod found; logs show Envoy start but no ECONNREFUSED lines. Priority-2: validated frontend-proxy runtime config and frontend Service — proxy env points to frontend:8080; Service exposes 8080 and has a healthy endpoint; mismatch between observed refused IP and current ClusterIP indicates stale address usage rather than config/port mismatch. Priority-3: inspected frontend backend pod — pod is Ready and serving on 8080, so backend process is healthy. Correlated findings point to stale address resolution/config in the proxy (Envoy) or cached DNS/ClusterIP as the mechanism for ECONNREFUSED. No evidence was found that the frontend pod or Service port configuration was incorrect.
